name: Shift Coverage vs Demand Check
value_proposition: Line up hourly POS demand against clocked hours under owner-set minimums and a 3-of-4-weeks pattern rule, so the manager sees which day-parts are repeatedly overstaffed or understaffed before editing next week's schedule — the Blueprint never posts a shift.
persona: Owner or general manager of a café, quick-service restaurant, retail shop, or fitness studio with 8-40 hourly staff. They use a POS and a scheduling or time-clock app and mostly copy each week's schedule from the last.
problem: Schedules follow habit instead of demand. Some slow hours have more staff than needed while rush hours run short, and nobody has time to line up sales by hour against clocked hours.
workflow: 1. The person writes staffing rules before any flag: minimum staff per open hour (or by role), a target range of transactions per staff-hour, roles that cannot be cut (such as the keyholder), and day-parts with non-sales work (prep, restocking, cleaning). PERSON DECIDES: the minimum, the target range, protected roles, and which quiet hours still need coverage for non-sales work.

2. The person exports 4-8 weeks of hourly transactions or sales from the POS, and clocked hours by hour from the time-clock or scheduling app, then removes employee names, pay rates, tax IDs, and other columns the workflow does not need. PERSON DECIDES: which columns to keep. This is an export review, not a live POS, scheduling, or time-clock connection.

3. The person checks the data settings of their AI assistant (chat history, training use, and file retention) before pasting or uploading anything. File upload support differs by ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini plan, account, and admin settings. PERSON DECIDES: whether to upload the file, paste the rows as text, or not use AI for this data at all.
4. The person pastes the Coverage Check Prompt and their rules from the Staffing Rules Worksheet, then attaches or pastes the aligned hourly rows.

5. AI calculates transactions per staff-hour for each day-part with every formula left visible as text. It flags a block only when the result is outside the owner's target range in at least 3 of the weeks in the export. It does not flag a single bad day. PERSON DECIDES: whether a flagged block is real enough to change the next schedule.

6. AI labels each point CONFIRMED (calculated from the exports), OWNER-ENTERED (minimum, target range, protected roles, non-sales day-parts), AI INTERPRETATION (possible causes the data cannot confirm, such as prep work missing from the POS), or RECOMMENDED ACTION (a coverage-safe shift move that never drops below the owner's minimum). It includes a reminder to check local scheduling and break rules. PERSON DECIDES: whether any schedule change happens.

7. The person uses the Schedule Change Review Checklist and checks every CONFIRMED transactions-per-staff-hour figure against the export rows. PERSON DECIDES: edit the next schedule in their own scheduling tool, or change nothing. The Blueprint never edits schedules, posts shifts, or contacts staff.

8. After about 4 weeks, the person pastes the Four-Week Re-Check Prompt with a new export for the same flagged blocks and records whether those blocks moved into the target range. PERSON DECIDES: whether to keep, reverse, or further adjust the schedule change.
before: The manager copies last week's schedule, feels short-handed on Saturday, sees staff idle on Tuesday afternoon, and has no numbers to justify a change.
after: The manager has a short list of day-parts that are overstaffed or understaffed in most weeks, each with its calculation, a coverage-safe suggestion, and a re-check four weeks later.

guided_demo.summary: A public, six-step walkthrough at /blueprints/ai-staffing-optimizer using a fictional café with 4 weeks of invented hourly sales and clocked hours (names already removed). Owner rules are minimum 2 on floor, target 15-25 transactions per staff-hour, and flag only if outside target in 3 or more of 4 weeks. Tue 14:00 is overstaffed in 4 of 4 weeks; Sat 12:00 is understaffed in 4 of 4 weeks. Clicking a flagged block shows visible formulas, the weeks that triggered it, and AI INTERPRETATION kept separate from the math. A coverage-safe recommendation stops at the minimum-staff rule. A mock four-week re-check shows Sat 12:00 moving into the target after adding one person. Confirmed facts, owner-entered rules, AI interpretation, and recommended actions are labelled with text, not color alone. Every hour, transaction count, and staff count is invented. No live POS, scheduling, or time-clock system is attached.
steps: Step 1 of 6 - The exports: show the fictional two-row hour table (Tue 14:00: week1_tx 12, week2_tx 10, week3_tx 11, week4_tx 11, week1_staff 4, week2_staff 4, week3_staff 4, week4_staff 4; Sat 12:00: week1_tx 90, week2_tx 82, week3_tx 88, week4_tx 92, week1_staff 3, week2_staff 3, week3_staff 3, week4_staff 3). Show rules text 'minimum 2 on floor', 'target 15-25', and 'flag only if outside target in 3+ of 4 weeks'. Label the table invented. State that no live POS, scheduling, or time-clock account is attached.

Step 2 of 6 - Owner rules first: show the exact heading 'OWNER RULES FIRST'. Show OWNER-ENTERED minimum '2', target range '15-25 transactions per staff-hour', protected role 'keyholder', and non-sales note that quiet hours may include prep. State that a single week outside the target is not enough to flag.

Step 3 of 6 - Day-by-hour grid and flags: show a grid with Tue 14:00 and Sat 12:00. Show CONFIRMED Tue formulas '=12/4' result '3.0', '=10/4' result '2.5', '=11/4' result '2.8', '=11/4' result '2.8', and text that Tue 14:00 is below the 15-25 target in 4 of 4 weeks (overstaffed pattern). Show CONFIRMED Sat formulas '=90/3' result '30.0', '=82/3' result '27.3', '=88/3' result '29.3', '=92/3' result '30.7', and text that Sat 12:00 is above target in 4 of 4 weeks (understaffed pattern). Mark over and under flags with visible text and an icon, not color alone. Show the text labels 'CONFIRMED', 'OWNER-ENTERED', 'AI INTERPRETATION', and 'RECOMMENDED ACTION' as visible words.

Step 4 of 6 - Check one flagged block: open the Tue 14:00 CONFIRMED line. A 'Check facts against the export row' button shows four week rows (week1 12 vs 12 and 4 vs 4; week2 10 and 4; week3 11 and 4; week4 11 and 4), each labelled with the text 'Matches'. Show AI INTERPRETATION text containing 'prep' and 'POS export does not show'.

Step 5 of 6 - Coverage-safe recommendation and re-check: show RECOMMENDED ACTION text containing 'consider 2 on floor Tue 14:00-15:00' and 'your minimum', and Sat text containing 'adding 1 person' and '88 / 4 = 22'. Show a mock four-week re-check where Sat 12:00 with 4 staff shows transactions per staff-hour inside 15-25 in 4 of 4 weeks, and Tue 14:00 with 2 staff remains below target with text that non-sales work may still apply. Show the sentence 'Re-check the same blocks after 4 weeks with a new export.'

Step 6 of 6 - You edit the schedule: state the exact sentences 'You edit the schedule in your own tool. The kit changes nothing.' and 'Do not cut below your minimum staff.' and 'Check local scheduling and break rules before changing posted shifts.' Explain that the person edits shifts in their own scheduling tool, or decides not to, and that nothing is sent, edited, cancelled, or paid automatically. Offer a link to the Premium kit labelled as private preview with sign-in required.

guided_demo.fictional_data_notice: All hours, transaction counts, staff counts, and dates on this page are fictional. No real business data is used, and nothing is connected to a POS, scheduling tool, time clock, or any other live system.

kit_contents.title: Coverage Check Setup Checklist
kit_contents.purpose: Step-by-step setup for one run. It covers writing the minimum staff rule, target transactions-per-staff-hour range, protected roles, and non-sales day-parts; exporting 4-8 weeks of hourly POS transactions and clocked hours with names removed; aligning hour buckets across systems; checking the AI tool's data settings before pasting or uploading; and the rule that this is an export review, not a live POS or scheduling connection. It notes that file upload support differs by ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini plan, account, and admin settings, and that rows can be pasted as text instead.

kit_contents.title: Coverage Check Prompt
kit_contents.purpose: Copyable prompt that writes OWNER RULES FIRST, calculates transactions per staff-hour with every formula visible, flags a day-part only when it is outside the owner's target in at least 3 of the weeks, never recommends staffing below the owner's minimum, labels CONFIRMED, OWNER-ENTERED, AI INTERPRETATION, and RECOMMENDED ACTION separately, and forbids editing schedules, posting shifts, contacting staff, inventing transaction counts, and inventing savings.

kit_contents.title: Four-Week Re-Check Prompt
kit_contents.purpose: Copyable prompt used only after about four weeks. It recalculates the previously flagged day-parts from a new export, compares whether each block moved into the target range, leaves formulas visible, and forbids inventing the new week numbers or editing the schedule.

kit_contents.title: Staffing Rules Worksheet
kit_contents.purpose: Browser-only form where the person sets minimum staff on floor, target transactions-per-staff-hour low and high, the pattern rule (default flag when outside target in 3 or more of 4 weeks), protected roles, and optional non-sales day-parts. It generates a copyable rules block to paste with the Coverage Check Prompt. Nothing is saved to Atlas.

kit_contents.title: Hourly Coverage Workbook Template
kit_contents.purpose: Column layout (day, hour, week1_tx through week4_tx, week1_staff through week4_staff, week1_tx_per_staff_formula through week4_tx_per_staff_formula, weeks_outside_target, flag, notes) with the fictional Tue 14:00 and Sat 12:00 demo numbers and visible formula text such as =12/4 and =90/3. Includes a Copy CSV button so the person can start their own spreadsheet.

kit_contents.title: Schedule Change Review Checklist
kit_contents.purpose: Interactive, session-only checklist used before changing the next schedule. It confirms that every CONFIRMED transactions-per-staff-hour figure matches the export rows, that flags used the 3-of-4 (or owner-set) pattern rule rather than a single week, that recommendations never drop below the minimum staff rule, that protected roles were not cut, that quiet hours with possible prep were not treated as confirmed overstaffing alone, that local scheduling and break rules were considered, and that the person edits the schedule in their own tool themselves.

kit_contents.title: Fictional Sample Hourly Export
kit_contents.purpose: The same fictional two-row hourly CSV and owner-entered rules used in the guided demo, labelled as fictional, with a Copy CSV button. The person can practice the full workflow in their AI tool before using real POS or time-clock data.

kit_contents.title: Data and Safety Guidance
kit_contents.purpose: Rules for handling POS and time-clock exports in AI tools: review data settings, remove employee names and pay rates, do not paste scheduling-system passwords, do not recommend coverage below a safe or legally required minimum, do not ignore non-sales work, do not invent savings or return-on-investment claims, remind the person to check local scheduling and break rules, and remember that nothing is edited or sent to staff automatically. It also states that file upload support differs by plan.

decision_rules: Write OWNER RULES FIRST and finish the arithmetic before any schedule-change suggestion or interpretation.
Transactions per staff-hour for a week equals that week's transactions divided by that week's staff count for the same day-part. Leave every formula visible as text (for example =12/4 and =90/3).
Flag a day-part only when transactions per staff-hour is outside the owner's target range in at least 3 of the weeks in the export (or the owner-set N-of-M pattern). Do not flag a single bad day.
Never recommend staffing below the owner's written minimum for that open hour. If a cut would break the minimum, say so and stop at the minimum.
Never recommend cutting a role on the owner's protected-role list (for example keyholder).
If a remaining row is missing day, hour, a week of transactions, or a week of staff, or staff is 0, do not include that week in the pattern count. List it under NEEDS YOUR CHECK.
Do not invent transaction counts, staff counts, savings, labor-cost percentages, or ROI. Use only values from the files and rules the person pasted.

A quiet POS hour is CONFIRMED low transactions per staff-hour only. Possible prep, restocking, or cleaning needs are AI INTERPRETATION unless the person labelled that day-part as non-sales work in the rules.

CONFIRMED means calculated from the exports. OWNER-ENTERED means minimum, target range, pattern rule, protected roles, or non-sales day-parts. AI INTERPRETATION is not a confirmed fact. RECOMMENDED ACTION is never executed by the kit.
Include a reminder to check local scheduling, break, and predictive-scheduling rules before changing posted shifts. The export cannot show those rules.

On a later run after about four weeks, recalculate the same previously flagged day-parts from a new export with visible formulas. Do not invent the new week numbers. If no new export was provided, say that no new export was provided.
human_ai_boundary: AI calculates transactions per staff-hour and applies the owner's pattern rule. The person decides the minimum staff, target range, protected roles, and non-sales day-parts.
AI flags only when a day-part is outside the target in enough weeks. The person decides whether a flag means the next schedule should change.

AI leaves every formula visible and labels CONFIRMED, OWNER-ENTERED, AI INTERPRETATION, and RECOMMENDED ACTION separately. The person checks every CONFIRMED number against the export rows before treating it as true.
AI may suggest coverage-safe shift moves that still respect the minimum and protected roles. The person decides whether any edit happens.
AI never connects to a POS, scheduling tool, or time clock, never edits a shift, never posts a shift, and never contacts staff. The person edits the schedule in their own tool, or decides not to.
AI recalculates previously flagged blocks only when the person provides a new export. Only the person records whether the change worked.
The person decides whether any recommended action happens.
safety: Nothing is sent, edited, cancelled, or paid automatically. Every page states that the person edits the schedule in their own tool and that the kit changes nothing.
Atlas does not connect to a POS, scheduling tool, time clock, payroll provider, or any other vendor. It has no OAuth flow, no API call, and does not upload the person's data to any third party.

Before pasting or uploading exports to an AI tool, the person is told to review that tool's data settings and to remove employee names, pay rates, tax IDs, and other columns the workflow does not need.
The kit tells the person not to paste scheduling-system passwords, bank account numbers, Social Security numbers, or full employee names into the AI tool.
File upload support and data controls in ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini differ by plan, account, and admin settings. The kit says so and does not claim any plan includes a specific capability.
The kit tells the person not to cut below minimum coverage or local scheduling rules, not to ignore non-sales work in quiet hours, and not to invent savings or ROI.
All demo and sample data is fictional and labelled as fictional on the page.
Worksheet entries and checklist progress stay in the browser session only and are not saved to Atlas.

The pages contain no invented statistics, savings, or ROI claims, and no price or checkout. The only counts and ratios are the fictional hourly math, owner-entered rules, and the fictional four-week re-check.
required_data_tools: POS hourly sales or transactions export (CSV)
Time-clock or scheduling export of hours by employee or role (CSV), with names removed
Owner-entered staffing rules (minimum staff, target transactions per staff-hour, protected roles, non-sales day-parts)
Spreadsheet (Google Sheets or Excel) so formulas stay visible
A file-capable AI assistant. File upload support differs by plan, account, and admin settings; rows can be pasted as text instead.

constraints: Private preview only. The guided demo lives at /blueprints/ai-staffing-optimizer and the Premium kit at /blueprints/ai-staffing-optimizer/kit. Both pages set robots noindex and are not linked from the homepage, header navigation, or the sitemap.

The Premium kit requires requireUser from src/lib/auth.ts and hasActiveEntitlement for this product. It is labelled "Premium · Private preview". It shows no Stripe price, checkout, or Buy Premium unless the product is already in PAID_PRODUCTS.
All sample data is fictional and labelled as fictional. No live connector, OAuth flow, API call, or upload to a third party.
AI prepares; the person decides. Confirmed facts, AI interpretation, and recommended actions are labelled separately. Nothing is sent, edited, cancelled, or paid automatically.
No invented statistics, savings, or ROI claims. ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini capabilities differ by plan; say so where it matters.

Product files live in app/blueprints/ai-staffing-optimizer/, components/premium/ai-staffing-optimizer/, and src/lib/premium/ai-staffing-optimizer/. Register the Blueprint in src/lib/blueprints.ts. Do not edit Daily Inbox, Collections product behavior, Stripe, or Production.
e2e/ai-staffing-optimizer/authenticated.spec.ts is read-only once it exists. Do not skip, weaken, or rewrite it. Authenticated QA uses automatic session refresh.
Keyboard accessible, visible labels, no horizontal scrolling at a phone-sized viewport, no console errors.
